worksheet.title: Growing Patterns
worksheet.subtitle: Patterns with three parts
worksheet.learning_goal: I can read a three-part pattern and keep it going.

parts.title: Some patterns have three parts
parts.text: This pattern repeats three shapes: triangle, square, circle. Read it out loud to hear how it repeats.

parts.title: Watch Bit — ▲ ■ ● ▲ ■ ● …
parts.note: It goes triangle, square, circle — then starts again. The next one is ▲.

parts.title: Draw what comes next
parts.prompt: Read the three-part pattern, then draw the next shape in the dashed box.

parts.title: Draw the next TWO
parts.prompt: Keep this pattern going. Draw the next two shapes in the dashed boxes.

parts.title: You try — make your own
parts.prompt: Pick two or three shapes (● ▲ ■ ★) and draw your own pattern that repeats.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: When you know a pattern, you can keep it going as long as you like. Computers use patterns to repeat steps again and again.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children read a three-part (ABC) repeating pattern, extend it by one and by two shapes, and create their own. Extending a pattern by more than one step builds prediction — a computational-thinking skill behind repeating a process.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children read, extend, and create repeating patterns.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child draws the shapes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil/crayon. Optional: pattern blocks or coloured beads to build ABC patterns by hand.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: say the three-part pattern aloud — 'triangle, square, circle…'. The next is a triangle.
2. GUIDED: do Exercise 1 together — ● ■ ★ repeating, the next is ●.
3. YOU TRY: children predict the next TWO in Exercise 2 (● then ▲), then create their own in Exercise 3.
4. Connect: 'Computers use patterns to repeat steps again and again — just like your pattern keeps going.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 3 — any pattern that truly repeats is correct (e.g. ★ ● ★ ● …, or ● ▲ ■ ● ▲ ■).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: in Ex 2, drawing only one shape — point to both dashed boxes.
Simplify: do two-part patterns first, then add the third shape.
Extend: ask the child to read their own pattern aloud and continue it for two more shapes.
Movement option: stomp–clap–jump, stomp–clap–jump — what three actions come next?

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child extends a three-part pattern correctly, draws two correct shapes in Exercise 2, and creates a pattern in Exercise 3 that genuinely repeats.
